findings.title: Type alias TakeTwo is overly generic and hard to read
findings.body: The new `TakeTwo` type alias is 18 lines long and uses complex conditional types to handle edge cases. It is not immediately clear what this type is for or why it is needed. Consider simplifying the type or adding a comment explaining its purpose and usage.

findings.title: Function devtoolsImpl is too long and complex
findings.body: The new `devtoolsImpl` function is 147 lines long and contains deeply nested logic. This violates rule 1 of 'Complex Function Improvement Suggestions' (split functions longer than 50 lines). Consider extracting smaller, focused functions to improve readability and maintainability.

findings.title: Error handling for window access is not robust
findings.body: The code attempts to access `window` without checking if it exists in a non-browser environment. This can lead to runtime errors in server-side rendering or non-browser contexts. Add a guard to check for the existence of `window` before accessing it.

findings.title: Error handling for devtools extension is not robust
findings.body: The code assumes the Redux DevTools extension is available and does not handle the case where it is not installed or enabled. This can lead to silent failures or unexpected behavior. Add proper error handling to warn the user and provide a fallback behavior.

findings.title: Type assertion for setState is unsafe
findings.body: The code uses a type assertion `(api.setState as NamedSet<S>)` to override the type of `setState`. This bypasses TypeScript's type safety and could lead to runtime errors if the types do not align. Consider refactoring to avoid type assertions.

summary.problem: The devtools middleware refactor introduces overly complex types, long functions, and fragile error handling that can break in non-browser environments or when the Redux DevTools extension is unavailable.
summary.done_well: The refactor modernizes the devtools middleware to use the new Zustand API and improves type safety in several areas. The changes are isolated to a single file and maintain backward compatibility for most use cases.
